questions.enonce_markdown: State FIVE transport functions of blood. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Transport functions of blood (any five):

1. Transports **oxygen** from the lungs to the body tissues (as oxyhaemoglobin in red blood cells).
2. Transports **carbon dioxide** from the tissues to the lungs (mainly as hydrogencarbonate in plasma).
3. Transports **digested food (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol, vitamins and mineral salts)** from the small intestine to the liver and to the cells.
4. Transports **nitrogenous waste (urea)** from the liver and tissues to the kidneys for excretion.
5. Transports **hormones** from the endocrine glands to the target organs.
6. Transports **heat** from the deep organs (such as the liver and muscles) to the skin and around the body.
7. Transports **antibodies and white blood cells** to the sites of infection.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the mechanism of blood clotting. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Blood clotting prevents loss of blood and entry of germs when a blood vessel is cut.

1. When a blood vessel is damaged, the **platelets** and the **damaged tissue cells** are exposed to air and **release an enzyme, thrombokinase (thromboplastin)**.
2. In the presence of **calcium ions** (and **vitamin K**, needed for the formation of the clotting factors in the liver), thrombokinase **converts the inactive plasma protein prothrombin into the active enzyme thrombin**.
3. **Thrombin converts the soluble plasma protein fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin**, in the form of long **threads**.
4. The **fibrin threads form a network (mesh)** across the wound which **traps red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets**, forming a **clot**.
5. The clot **dries and hardens to form a scab**, which **seals the wound** and prevents entry of micro-organisms and further bleeding; under the scab the tissue heals.

*Summary*: prothrombin becomes thrombin (thrombokinase and Ca$^{2+}$ needed); fibrinogen becomes fibrin (thrombin needed); fibrin + blood cells = clot.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State FOUR differences between:

(i) Arteries and veins

(ii) Blood and lymph. *(4, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Arteries and veins** (any four differences)

| Arteries | Veins |
|---|---|
| Carry blood **away from the heart**. | Carry blood **towards the heart**. |
| Carry **oxygenated blood** (except the pulmonary artery). | Carry **deoxygenated blood** (except the pulmonary vein). |
| Blood flows under **high pressure**, in pulses. | Blood flows under **low pressure**, smoothly. |
| **Thick, muscular and elastic walls**; **narrow lumen**. | **Thin walls** with few muscle and elastic fibres; **wide lumen**. |
| **No valves** (except at the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery). | **Valves** are present to prevent backflow. |

(ii) **Blood and lymph** (any four differences)

| Blood | Lymph |
|---|---|
| Contains **red blood cells** (and white cells and platelets). | **No red blood cells** and no platelets; has only **white cells (lymphocytes)**. |
| Is **red** (haemoglobin). | Is **colourless or pale yellow**. |
| Has a **higher concentration of proteins, oxygen and digested food**. | Has **less protein, oxygen and food**, but more waste such as carbon dioxide. |
| Flows in **blood vessels (a closed system)**, pumped by the heart. | Flows in **lymph vessels**, moved by body movements (no pump); it flows **in one direction only** and ends in the veins. |
| Clots quickly. | **Clots slowly**. |
